title: Extractor run and output
statement: Let $x$ and $r$ be Boolean words, and write $x=p r$ for a split into a prefix $p$ and suffix $r$. For any Boolean flags and any buffered Boolean word $a$, there is a time $t \le 3|r|+2|a|+5$ at which the pair extractor, started in its initial extraction state with input head just past $p$, buffer $a$, work head at $|a|$, and empty output, is halted. Its output is $(a b)$ when the first flag is true, followed by $c$ when the second flag is true, if $r$ decodes as the pair $(b,c)$; if $r$ does not decode, its output is empty.
hypotheses_covered: A prefix p with x = p ++ r
replaced:
For any split $x = p s$ of the input and any buffered prefix $a$, there is a
time $t \le 3\abs{s} + 2\abs{a} + 5$ such that after $t$ steps from the
block-start state at position $\abs{p}$ the extractor has halted; if $s$
decodes under the self-delimiting pair code as $(b,c)$, the output is $a b$
(when the first flag is set) followed by $c$ (when the second flag is set),
and if $s$ is not a valid pair code the output is empty.
